Hi, welcome to my homepage!

I'm Cheng Chen, a Communication Engineering undergraduate at Tongji University, expecting to graduate in June 2027. I am an incoming Ph.D. student at the Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences, with an expected start in September 2027 under the supervision of Prof. Kaiqi Huang.

I study how models learn from complementary sources of information and how to make that knowledge useful under limited compute. My work spans knowledge distillation, audio-visual understanding, and multimodal evaluation. I also build software for literature discovery and other research workflows.

Research Interests

  • Multimodal learning and audio-visual understanding
  • Large language models and multimodal large language models
  • Embodied AI and reinforcement learning
  • Efficient AI, knowledge distillation, model compression, and lightweight deployment

Publications

* Equal contribution · Corresponding author indicated where applicable.

If You Hear It, Help Find It: Orthogonal Knowledge Distillation for Open-Vocabulary Audio-Visual Event Localization

Cheng Chen*, Yi Xu*, Wenzhuo Lei (* equal contribution)

ACM Multimedia (ACM MM) 2026

We study open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization when visual and audio teachers differ in reliability. OV-OrthKD places their supervision in separate orthogonal feature paths and uses text prototypes for open-vocabulary transfer.

OrthKD: Extracting Generalized Clinical Knowledge from Heterogeneous Teachers for Lightweight Deployment

Yi Xu*, Cheng Chen*, Mufan Cao (* equal contribution)

International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI) 2026

We study multi-teacher distillation for diabetic retinopathy screening. OrthKD transfers complementary feature-level knowledge from heterogeneous teachers to a 5.4M-parameter MobileNetV3 student.

Enabling Visual Reasoning in Text-Only LLMs via Symbolic Scene Descriptions

Wenzhuo Lei, Mufan Cao, Chaorong Ye, Yi Xu, Cheng Chen

International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN) 2026 Corresponding Author

We convert images into grammar-constrained scene descriptions that can be processed by a text-only LLM. On VQAv2, DeepYOLO achieves 42.3% accuracy while using 2.5× fewer prompt tokens than scene-graph serialization.

Generated Image Evaluation

AAAI 2027 Under Review · Phase 2

Research on assessing whether generated images satisfy textual instructions, with a focus on reliable evaluation.

Reliability in Model Interpretability

ICLR 2027 Submitted

Research on evaluating the evidence used to explain neural-network behavior and the reliability of the resulting interpretations.

Understanding and Generation in Multimodal Models

ICLR 2027 Submitted

Research on how learning in visual understanding relates to image-generation behavior in multimodal models.

Reliability of Neural Operator Predictions

ICLR 2027 Submitted

Research on identifying unreliable predicted physical fields efficiently, with a focus on neural operators and single-pass risk assessment.
